cim_eredeti: Is Canva Free? What the Free Plan and Canva AI Include in 2026
szoveg_eredeti:
Yes, Canva is free — and the free plan is a real product, not a trial. Canva Free gives you the drag-and-drop editor, 1.6 million templates, 4.7 million stock items, 5GB of storage, and one Brand Kit at US$0, as of September 2026. What is not free is most of the AI: Canva Free includes a shared allowance of up to 20 Standard or Premium AI uses a month, no Ultra AI, and no Canva AI 2.0. Everything above that sits in Canva Pro (US$144 a year for one person) or Canva Business (US$250 a year per person). This guide answers the questions people ask most, with numbers from Canva’s own pages, then shows where a dedicated image generator like Krea fits beside Canva rather than instead of it.

Canva figures come from Canva’s pricing page and AI usage article, checked September 2026; the Business monthly price is from Canva’s launch announcement. Krea figures are from krea.ai/pricing. Canva shows yearly prices by default (yearly “saves from 16%”); we could not render the monthly Pro price, so we do not quote one.

Every price, quota, and plan boundary was checked against Canva’s published pages in September 2026: the pricing page, Understanding your AI usage, Get started with Canva AI, the AI quality tiers article, the upgrade guide, and the commercial use guide. For ChatGPT we used OpenAI’s Free tier FAQ. Where a vendor publishes no exact number, we say so. Every example image is a single, raw Krea 2 generation from the exact prompt beside it; none were made with Canva or ChatGPT.

Canva Free is free for as long as you use it. Per Canva’s pricing page, it includes the editor and 1,000+ design types, 1.6 million+ templates, 4.7 million+ photos, videos, graphics, and audio clips, one Brand Kit limited to 3 colors, 5GB of storage, PDF/JPG/PNG export, and Canva Offline.

What Free leaves out: the 3.6 million premium templates and 141 million premium stock items (crown-marked in the editor), extra Brand Kits, social scheduling, 100GB of storage, Ultra AI tools, and Canva AI 2.0. Canva’s help center says Free users “can access Canva AI 1.0 features and some AI tools like Magic Write and Background Remover with limited monthly usage.” Background removal is one of those limited tools; if you do it often, try Krea’s background remover or see the best AI background removers in 2026.

Commercial use is not a paid feature. Canva’s commercial use guide allows Free and Pro content in original designs you sell, as long as you do not resell Canva’s stock on its own.

Canva Free recipe (no image here — we don’t fake Canva outputs):

Sign up at canva.com. Choose Instagram Post, search templates for “minimal product launch”, pick one without a crown icon, replace the photo with your own upload, and export as PNG. Nothing in this flow touches your AI allowance.

Variation tips: filter the template panel to free-only results; upload your own photos to keep the design original for commercial use.

Yes, with a hard monthly cap. Canva meters every AI feature through one shared “AI allowance.” Canva’s AI usage article gives these estimates:

Three details matter on Free. The numbers are “up to” estimates for simple tasks; complex prompts use more. Standard tools count too — Magic Write, Canva AI text, the Image Upscaler, and Standard-quality images all draw from the same 20-use pool. And the allowance resets at 12:00 a.m. UTC on the first of each month. When you run out, Canva’s AI quality tiers article says all tiers become unavailable until the reset. One trap: Pro and Business free trials carry the same allowance as Canva Free; per the upgrade guide, the 10x allowance “becomes available once your trial converts to a paid plan.”

Open Canva AI from the side navigation, select the + (Attachments) icon, choose AI quality → Standard, pick Image, and prompt: “Flat-lay photo of a ceramic mug and a notebook on a linen cloth, soft daylight, muted colors.” Standard quality uses the least of your 20 monthly uses.

Variation tips: write the full brief in one prompt — every regeneration is another use; keep Premium quality for the final image.

“Canva AI” now means two things. Canva AI 1.0 is the single-prompt generator: choose Design, Image, Doc, Code, or Video clip and get a result you open in the editor. Canva AI 2.0, launched at Canva Create 2026, is a conversational assistant inside the editor that refines whole multi-page designs, keeps them on brand, remembers preferences through a Memory Library, runs web research, and connects to outside tools. It is available with Pro, Teams, Business, and Nonprofit plans; Free users stay on 1.0. The pricing page sorts the features into Standard AI (Magic Write, Magic Formulas, Standard-quality images), Premium AI (design, element, and video generation, Canva Code, Magic Layers, Image to Video), and Ultra AI (conversational design with 2.0, high-quality video clips, Ultra-quality images; paid only).

Where it stops: Canva AI is a design assistant, not an image model you control. You cannot pick the model, set a seed, feed a style reference, or train it on your own work. Quality is a Standard/Premium/Ultra menu, and Ultra costs Pro users 20 uses a month. Canva’s job is the finished post or deck; it is not built for exploring a hundred variations of one image.

Create a 5-slide pitch deck for a neighborhood coffee roaster: who we are, our beans, wholesale pricing, three customer quotes, contact. Warm cream and espresso brown palette, one idea per slide, leave placeholders for real numbers.

Variation tips: name the palette and slide count; “leave placeholders” stops it inventing figures. For deck tools compared, see the best AI PPT makers in 2026.

Canva’s pricing page lists Canva Pro at US$144 a year for one person, with monthly billing at a higher rate. Pro adds premium templates and stock, 5 Brand Kits, social scheduling, 100GB, Canva AI 2.0, and the 200-Premium-or-20-Ultra allowance. Canva Business is US$250 a year per person, or US$20 per person per month per Canva’s announcement, with no seat minimum; it adds team admin, 100 Brand Kits with approvals, 500GB, and double Pro’s AI allowance. Canva Teams is “no longer available for new sign-ups or upgrades.” For more AI, Canva sells AI Pass (“40x more AI than Canva Pro”) and AI top-ups (a 30-day boost for Business) at extra cost; the pricing page does not list their prices.

Count your AI generations in a normal month. Under 20 → Free. 20 to 200 Premium generations, or you need premium templates and Brand Kits → Pro. A team, or 200+ → Business. If images are the bottleneck rather than layouts, compare a generation-first tool before buying AI Pass.

They overlap on one feature: making an image from a sentence. ChatGPT is a general assistant that also generates images; Canva AI is a design assistant that generates images as one step toward a layout.

Where ChatGPT wins. OpenAI’s Free tier FAQ confirms Free users can “Create images in ChatGPT.” Its image model follows long, specific briefs closely and renders in-image text well; see ChatGPT vs Midjourney. Where it stops: OpenAI publishes no daily image number for Free — the FAQ says image generation has “separate usage limits” that “can have stricter limits than paid plans” — and the output is a single image with no layout or brand kit around it.

Where Canva AI wins. The result lands in an editable design on your brand colors, and Canva AI 2.0 can revise a whole deck through conversation. Where it stops: 20 uses a month on Free is fewer image experiments than most people run in a week, and Free never reaches the Ultra quality tier.

ChatGPT image recipe (no image here — we don’t fake ChatGPT outputs):

In a free ChatGPT account type: “Generate a 16:9 image: flat-lay photo of a ceramic mug and a notebook on a linen cloth, soft daylight, muted colors, no text.” If you hit the limit, ChatGPT shows the reset time.

Variation tips: ask for one change per follow-up; each edit is a new generation against the same limit.

cim: Havonta csak 20 AI-generálást ad ingyen a Canva
lead: Bár a Canva ingyenes verziója továbbra is használható, az AI-eszközök havi 20 alkalmas korlátot kaptak, a Canva AI 2.0 pedig csak előfizetéssel érhető el.
osszefoglalo:
A Canva ingyenes csomagja továbbra is ingyenes marad, de az AI-funkciók használatát **havi 20 alkalmas közös keretre** korlátozzák. Ez a limit a Standard és Premium AI-eszközökre, például a [Magic Write](https://www.canva.com/help/using-canva-ai/)-ra és a háttéreltávolítóra is vonatkozik. Az ingyenes verzió emellett 5 GB tárhelyet, 1,6 millió sablont és egy 3 színre korlátozott arculati készletet biztosít.

A fejlettebb, beszélgetős [Canva AI 2.0 asszisztens](https://www.canva.com) kizárólag a fizetős Pro és Business csomagokban érhető el. A Pro előfizetés évente 144 dollárba kerül, és havi 200 Premium vagy 20 Ultra AI-generálást tartalmaz. A 250 dolláros éves díjú Business csomag ehhez képest dupla AI-keretet és 500 GB tárhelyet ad a felhasználóknak.

Az ingyenes felhasználók kereskedelmi célra is használhatják a terveiket, de a generálási limit átlépése után az AI-eszközök a következő hónap elsejéig elérhetetlenné válnak. A korlátok miatt a komolyabb képgenerálási feladatokhoz érdemes lehet külső eszközöket, például a [Krea](https://www.krea.ai) felületét használni.
miert_szamit: A szűkös ingyenes keret miatt a marketingeseknek **pontosan meg kell tervezniük az AI-generálásokat**, mert a rontott próbálkozások is fogyasztják a limitet. Ha rendszeresen generálsz képeket vagy prezentációkat, **fel kell készülnöd a Pro előfizetésre** vagy egy dedikált képgeneráló eszköz használatára.
